title: cairn check retrieval evaluation set
filed_under: CAIRN-247 (spike: cairn check is English-stemmed word overlap, and half the corpus is French)
readme: WHAT THIS IS. Twenty real questions an agent would type into `cairn check` before
starting work, each paired with the rows that are the known-good answers. The refs
were verified by hand against the live store on 2026-09-21: every expected ref
exists and genuinely answers the question. The queries are deliberately NOT copies
of the titles — an agent asking the mandatory first-gate question does not know the
wording of the row it is hoping to find. That is the whole point: retrieval is only
worth measuring on paraphrase.
WHY IT EXISTS. CAIRN-247 says: 'Collect twenty such queries with their known-good
answers and score whatever is built against them, or we will ship embeddings and
have no idea whether they helped.' This is that set. Score BEFORE and AFTER any
change to the search configuration (language config, pgvector, ranking) and compare.
HOW TO SCORE. For each case, run the query through search and take the ordered list
of refs it returns (`cairn check "<query>" --json` -> results[].ref, 20 rows max,
or call search_all directly). Then, per case:
hit@k       = 1 if any expectedRefs[] appears in the first k results, else 0
rank        = 1-based position of the first expectedRef, or null if absent
reciprocal  = 1/rank, or 0 if absent  (MRR is the mean of these)
precise     = 1 if that hit came back with loose=false (i.e. it matched the
websearch_to_tsquery precise arm, not the widened OR fallback)
Report four numbers over the twenty cases: recall@20, recall@5, MRR, and the share
of cases whose hit was precise rather than widened. Report them split by
`lang` too — the French and cross-lingual subsets are the ones under suspicion, and
an aggregate that mixes them hides exactly the effect being measured.
WHAT COUNTS AS A REGRESSION. Any change that raises the French numbers while
dropping recall@20 on the `en` subset is not an improvement, it is a trade. The
'simple' text-search configuration is the obvious instance: it does no stemming at
all, so English plurals stop matching singulars and gerunds stop matching stems.
The `en` subset exists to price that loss, not to pad the count.
MAINTENANCE. Expected refs rot: a task can be merged, a knowledge entry superseded.
If a case stops being answerable, fix the case, do not delete it — a query with no
good answer left is a different measurement from a query the engine missed.

baseline.how: cairn check "<query>" --json against the live store, first expectedRef's 1-based position in results[]
baseline.system: Postgres FTS, search_all() as of migrations/033, every tsvector and tsquery built with the 'english' configuration, no embeddings
findings: 20 of 22 queries widened: the precise websearch_to_tsquery arm is not how this system answers a natural-language question, it is the exception.

The French subset scores BEST, not worst (recall@20 0.92 vs 0.43 for English). French content words are high-IDF against a mostly-English corpus, and the widening arm already drops words of 3 characters or fewer, which is most French function words.

Both non-widened queries (en-05, en-07) MISSED. Three or more irrelevant rows satisfied the AND query, so the widened arm was suppressed by p_min_precise. Re-running en-07 with --kinds knowledge drops the precise count below 3, the widening fires, and the correct entry comes back at rank 1 — same corpus, same query.
Re-measure with this file rather than trusting these numbers; they are a snapshot of a store that keeps growing.

cases.query: erreur de label Langfuse entre staging et production sur les prompts SMS
cases.why: HM-708 'Fix: les prompts SMS de production composaient leurs blocs communs via label=staging' is exactly this bug, already fixed. An agent that misses it re-debugs a solved production incident.

cases.query: relancer une seconde chance depuis une session d'entrainement deja terminee
cases.why: HERMES-110 is the audit of precisely this ('depuis une session d'entraînement TERMINÉE : possible, 5 verrous'); 105 and 109 are the adjacent work. Note the query is written without accents, as an agent on a US keyboard would type it — under an accent-sensitive index that alone is a miss.

cases.query: le persona parle tout seul et n'entend pas le conseiller
cases.why: Three separate recorded incidents of the V4 persona taking both sides of the call. The most-repeated failure in the HERMES corpus and entirely in French.

cases.query: mauvaise version de prompt affichee apres un rejeu
cases.why: HM-712/711 are the 'Versions du prompt' banner ignoring step replays. A paraphrase with no shared content word beyond 'version' and 'rejeu'.

cases.query: trop de zones de defilement imbriquees dans le configurateur
cases.why: SWV-251 'sortir des zones de scroll imbriquées et baisser la densité'. Tests the scroll/défilement synonym and, under any config, the accentless spelling.

cases.query: atteindre les offres derriere un ecart dans la vue lot de l'auditeur
cases.why: SWV-250, a near-restatement of the title with different word order and one synonym. If FTS misses this, it is the function words and the morphology, not the vocabulary.

cases.query: claude-mem consomme tout le quota d'abonnement
cases.why: CCS-27 'claude-mem brûle le quota d'abonnement'. 'consomme' vs 'brûle' is the kind of substitution no stemmer bridges and an embedding does.

cases.query: reduire le gaspillage de lecture de fichiers pendant une session
cases.why: CCS-26 is the measured read-waste work (DIS-2129). Close paraphrase, French, accentless — the easiest French case in the set, so a miss here is damning.

cases.query: quelle est la difference entre replay et rejouer dans la bibliotheque
cases.why: A knowledge entry written to answer exactly this question. If `cairn know` cannot return it for the question it was written for, the memory is write-only.

cases.query: pourquoi un rejeu tourne encore sur l'ancien prompt apres la promotion
cases.why: 'Un rejeu lancé juste après une promotion Langfuse tourne sur l'ANCIEN prompt (cache in-process)'. High-value: getting this wrong sends an agent debugging Langfuse for an hour.

cases.query: comment savoir si une analyse a ete rejouee
cases.why: The entry answers the question directly ('la preuve du rejeu est dans steps[]'). Passé composé in the query against infinitive/noun forms in the entry — the French morphology case in its purest form.

cases.query: quels prompts SMS ne sont plus utilises et peuvent etre archives
cases.why: Three consecutive tasks that audited, archived and deleted unused SMS prompts. An agent asking this is about to redo an audit that closed last week.

cases.query: SMS prompts in production were composing their shared blocks with the staging label
cases.why: Same fact as fr-01, asked in English about work recorded in French. Lexical search cannot answer this at all except through the loan words ('SMS', 'staging', 'production'); an embedding can. This case is the clearest discriminator between option 1 and option 2 in the spike.

cases.query: replaying an analysis right after promoting a prompt uses the cached old version
cases.why: English question, French entry, only 'Langfuse' and 'cache' shared. Second discriminator.

cases.query: the training persona answers for the adviser as well as itself
cases.why: English phrasing of fr-03. 'conseiller' -> 'adviser' is a translation, not a stem; measures the ceiling of lexical retrieval over a bilingual corpus.

cases.query: agents finish work without ever claiming the task, and nothing notices
cases.why: The case from the CAIRN-247 session: both refs are the right answers and both ranked below unrelated rows, found only because a human recognised the titles.

cases.query: can we tell whether the memory actually gave an agent the right answer
cases.why: CAIRN-254 is that exact question, filed and partly built. Paraphrase with 'recall'/'telemetry' deliberately absent.

cases.query: links in knowledge entries that point at something nobody ever wrote
cases.why: 'Two thirds of dangling knowledge references point at facts Cairn already holds'. The query avoids the words 'dangling' and 'reference' on purpose.

cases.query: detect when the installed CLI is older than the server it talks to
cases.why: 'A stale CLI only confesses if you ask it: --version is the one command that checks'. Tests 'stale' <-> 'older'.

cases.query: does clearing the context still record what the session did
cases.why: A knowledge entry written for this question. 'clearing' vs 'clear' is the plain English stemming case — it must keep working under any language-config change.

cases.query: grepping the porcelain output of git blame returns no commits
cases.why: Gerund against verb ('grepping'/'grep'), plural against singular ('commits'/'commit'). This case exists to price the loss of English stemming if the config moves to 'simple'.

cases.query: AWS list calls returning partial results without any error
cases.why: Plural 'calls' against 'call', 'returning' against 'return', and 'partial results' against 'plausible wrong answer'. Second pricing case for English stemming.
